key_insight: A causal reinforcement learning multimodal model combines chest X-rays with physician-written histories to improve both MACE risk prediction and clinical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This could help opportunistic cardiovascular risk screening from routinely collected data, potentially flagging higher-risk patients earlier across care settings.
method: Separates reasoning and risk prediction with a role-decoupled dual-LLM design.
Uses dual-action causal reinforcement learning to choose evidence and refine reasoning.
Applies causal token pruning to build compact multimodal representations.
evidence_signal: In internal, emergency department, and external MIMIC cohorts, the model achieved AUROCs of 0.720, 0.760, and 0.845, while also improving GREEN scores and expert preference.
watch_item: Performance and reasoning quality should still be validated prospectively before use in real-world workflows, especially across sites and patient populations.
paper_title: From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning
